---
title: "Sensitivity to costs, weights and grade restrictions"
subtitle: "4.10 · settings and sensitivity after the postrank vignette a7"
description: "Separate effects of changing the reporting loss and the feasible report family."
---

Withholding costs and error weights specify the reporting loss. A grade cap specifies the feasible family. The
exact path varies the withholding cost while holding the posterior, weights and family fixed. A separate grid
evaluates every combination of the declared costs, caps and weights. These displays distinguish changes in the
objective from changes in admissible reports. Criterion profiles and disclosure describe the consequences without
assuming that risks under different losses are directly comparable. The archived examples retain their recorded
settings and provide discrete sensitivity comparisons rather than continuous change points.

## Numerical illustrations {#what-to-try}

- **Equal weights.** The best report states 9 of 15 pairs. Its wrong shares are .0177 and .0267 on scores A and B.
  The exact path gives its interval and all returned equal-risk alternatives at the boundary costs.
- **A higher price.** The report states 11 pairs; score B’s wrong share is .115. A larger withholding cost can favour additional statements, even though some statements are less certain.
- **A still higher price.** The report states 12 pairs, while score B’s wrong share falls to .0575. Disclosure
  cannot fall along this fixed-family exact path; a criterion-specific wrong share can move either way.
- **At most two grades.** The best report states 8 pairs with risk .0939. The table that changes only the cap
  keeps the same price and weights, making its risks comparable; the smallest risk cannot rise as the family expands.
- **Thirty-site archive.** Recorded disclosures include 131, 276, 305 and 312 pairs. These dots describe the saved
  solves at their recorded prices. Their spacing does not locate the exact transitions of a continuous path.
- **Tutorial archive.** The package’s prepared sensitivity analysis has 7 settings, changing one setting at a time.
  The live view instead evaluates the full Cartesian grid with a fixed reference grade.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
Every row’s comparison reevaluates the same reference grade under that row’s loss. A reference excluded by a cap
remains a fixed-report comparator; it does not become an admissible solution. Across changed prices or weights,
risk values measure different losses. The thirty-site archives use joint draws and fixed settings, separately
from the Gaussian marginal example. Intervals and boundary tables belong to the live exact path; archived dots
carry their saved statuses and gaps. The R block below reads the prepared one-at-a-time tutorial archive.
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="In postrank"}
```r
library(postrank)
s <- readRDS(system.file("extdata/cached/tutorial_sensitivity.rds", package="postrank", mustWork=TRUE))$value
s$table[, c("setting_id", "risk", "N")]
```
:::

Standalone: [choosing-settings](../../embed/choosing-settings.html), for example `?preset=tau40&theme=dark`.
